items.quote: Asana supports the authorization code grant flow
items.why: Directly names OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant, the oauth2 method.

items.quote: Asana uses OAuth 2.0 for secure user authorization.
items.why: States Asana uses OAuth 2.0, which is the oauth2 method in the claim.

items.quote: A personal access token (PAT) is the quickest and simplest way to authenticate in the API.
items.why: Says PAT is the simplest auth route; never says bearer or lists it as a method.

items.quote: Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token.
items.why: Says review is not required, which contradicts the admin_approval gate claim.

items.quote: Limits are based on minute-long windows and differ depending on whether the domain is free or paid
items.why: About rate-limit window length; says nothing about credential gating or approval.

items.quote: Asana apps use features like our rest API, app components, and webhooks.
items.why: Lists REST API among app features; does not establish REST as primary or breadth of API.

items.quote: The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.
items.why: Gives the MCP V2 server URL and says it is available, so it exists.

items.quote: This server requires authentication with your Asana account.
items.why: Says server needs Asana auth; related to the MCP server but does not establish existence, official status or URL.
